questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not get accepted for my first priority, but I was very pleased to be accepted on Alexandria University instead, and really enjoyed my stay there. It of course had to be a destination where I would be able to speak arabic every day outside of my studies as well, because I study Middle Eastern Languages and Societies with arabic as my chosen language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: i would say it was easy, we were notified via email in advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were offered to be picked up at the airport, and in general they encouraged us to contact them if we experienced any issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: there were a lot of opportunities and apartments because we had contact information for brokers from other students who have been on exchange before. it wasn't easy to find good places where we could live mixed genders, and in general the quality of the apartments was different from place to place, but i found a very nice apartment after staying for a week in the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It has been very nice finding something independently, but you should definitely always check everything thoroughly in the apartment before signing or paying anything, as a lot of places have a problem with the water temperatures or the wifi or a broken fridge or the like, and it might not get properly fixed even if you point it out. This is from other's experiences and not mine though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It went smoothly as far as I remember, as we weren't many students, and it was easy to communicate with the administrative workers at the university

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure what is meant, but the help was sufficient if i remember correctly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This was no problem, as it was a mandatory stay with pretty much fixed subjects. the others from copenhagen, same semester, all took the same classes as i did for this reason so it was very easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm pretty sure it's easy to communicate with the Tafl center about subjects so contact them and ask what is available

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I do wish our Egyptian dialect class had been split into two levels, for the sake of everyone, as we had very different levels in the language in general, even though we had never had dialect classes. I didn't get challenged much, and people on lower levels felt that it moved very fast and got difficult very quickly. it would have been better to have two classes.
Also in the litterature class, I would have liked to work with more pieces of litterature, more material, as we moved a bit slowly. when i suggested this or other things, i would have liked for the teacher to have listened more to this feedback.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: it was BA level, and i had the higher level in the classes where we were divided in levels. this was a very good way.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I found the teachers very encouraging and competent, and they very well knew the struggle of learning a new language, because they're so used to work with foreigners. This was very nice and positive. Sometimes there was of course a language barrier, but it wasn't a big issue for me, I think it worked out good.
From some teachers at UCPH, i've unfortunately experienced less encouragement and patience, which i don't view as a good teaching strategy. It intimidates and it worsens the gaps in level, so did really like being at Alexandria university and experiencing a different teaching style.
This doesn't apply to all my teachers/professors at UCPH, but a few.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fusha, modern standard arabic.    7,5 ects
egyptian colloqial arabic.    15 ects
arabic litterature.    7,5 ects

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It was a mandatory stay with pretty fixed subjects, so i would of course recommend these, and if you havent had these subjects before, and they match your arabic level, then it definitely makes sense to do these courses.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
My phone bill back home was not able to be paused, so i had to pay that on top of my egyptian phone bill. The insurance of course cost a bit.
It was super cold when we arrived, so we had to buy thick blankets (dyner) to sleep with. For instance having to buy bottled water all the time as well was not something I'd thought about beforehand.
the residency card was 150 dollars on top of our regular visa of 25 dollars, so this cost a bit, but we were told in advance. 
because i was in egypt though, these things were not very expensive, so it was fine - it was more costly the trips we went on. But i did also try to save a lot of money and not spend so much during the trip.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were less expensive than anticipated, and for instance the flight tickets weren't so expensive.  Some things were much cheaper than in denmark, and then other things were almost the same price as in denmark, but that would for instance be danish butter. it was mostly not expensive unless you experiences someone wanting a higher price from you because you obviously was a tourist.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there was a singing club, a cinema club, a cooking club and a calligraphy club - and other events in the city, that teachers would let us know about

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
i attended them all, and enjoyed it. 
i would especially recommend cooking club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To see more of the city and more of egypt - and grab any opportunity that you have the energy for, to experience new areas, foods, cities, meet new people etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it wasn't very hard, but i've also visited the country before. people are very nice and curious and happy to answer your questions when you have any. people can also be a bit too approaching, which is annoying, but it's okay to say no, and to say you're not interested in talking

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: i wish i had done this more, so i dont have advice. but maybe there are events you can attend, and people are so open and talkative mostly, that i would recommend to just go op to someone and ask them about themselves and introduce yourself. and to try to find the people that you really want to become friends with, because that will be such a great thing to take with you, a new friendship

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: that women are not as present in the streets and out and about, and they're not as approaching as men - so it's harder to find female friends than male friends in egypt. and in general there is a lot of sexism, that i've experienced, a lot of cat calling and so on, which is definitely the biggest challenge for me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness and warmheartedness of people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: not sure

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not sure

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the language improvement and the experiences and trips, and my relations to people i met during the semester.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The experience of being a woman, knowing how much different everyday would have been as a man.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: in general a very good stay though, i really have enjoyed it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
